opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Black (E008) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, maximum is write unless her role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for Karen Black (E008): contractor with basic security training. Contractors cannot be granted admin, and write requires advanced training, so maximum level is read. Requested admin to Source Code; recommend granting read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin on Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer, and Karen is a Payroll Specialist, so her role does not own the system — admin is not permitted under either policy. The security record states she is a contractor with basic security training, so her maximum is read (write requires advanced training; contractors can never be admin). Since the request exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum of read. (Note: the HR note lists her as full_time, which would allow write; however, per the security record, contractor status with basic training applies, so read is the compliant level.)
